hardware_answers.question: Does kismet.datasource.channel follow the hops with the current C helper (local and remote) and with the Python remote helper, instead of staying at 6?

answers.answer: No. kismet.datasource.channel stays at the start channel (6 Wi-Fi, 15 zigbee, 37 btle) in C local, C remote and Python remote, while the helpers send CHANNELS 5 times a second. The wiki's 'may keep showing' should become 'keeps showing'. The code comment in chancontrol_callback claiming the framework reports it is wrong for Kismet's view.
answers.evidence: n1c {'6':600}, g4 {'6':1197}, n8b {('6',1):300} with 156 CHANNELS writes, n1d {('6',1):200} with 100 CHANNELS writes.

answers.answer: No. kismet.datasource.channel does not follow the hops for Python remote sources (nor for C local and C remote). It stays at the start channel: 6 for Wi-Fi, 15 for zigbee, 37 for BTLE.
answers.evidence: p2a polled REST at 5 Hz for 45 s (225 samples): {('6',1):225}, {('15',1):225}, {('37',1):225}. In 20 s, strace of the Python helper showed 100 CHANNELS writes on each of the Wi-Fi and zigbee fds, i.e. 5 per second. p4b/p9 show the same for C remote and C local.

hardware_answers.question: Does a board on the sibling's 1.2.0 web-flasher image sync and capture Wi-Fi, zigbee and btle under both final helpers? What are the BTLE fix-up behaviour and message text, and the length checks (no false drops)?

answers.answer: Yes, on the Kismet side (the extcap part, id 130, was not run). Board D8:0C on the published 1.2.0 image synced and captured all three radios under the C local, C remote and Python remote helpers. Wi-Fi: 792 / 516 / 342 packets. Zigbee: 200/200 TXTEST frames each, link type 230. BTLE: 2536 / 1141 / 633 packets, with 13/12/12 devices. The board sends flags 0x0013 and a zero CRC. Every helper rewrites each record to 0x0C13 with a valid CRC (100% of 4,323 pcapng packets checked) and logs this once per helper connection, verbatim: '<name>: the board's firmware does not mark BTLE packets as CRC checked, so Kismet would drop them; the helper fills in the CRC and the flags (the board only reports packets whose CRC passed). Flashing current firmware makes this unnecessary'. In Kismet it reads 'INFO: esp32c5btle-ttyACM2: ...' for a local source and 'INFO: esp32c5btle-ttyACM2 - esp32c5btle-ttyACM2: ...' for a remote one. There were 0 'impossible length' drops and 0 error packets. The only differences from current firmware are the fix-up message and the 0x0013 flags on the wire.
answers.evidence: f10w.out, f10z.out, f10b.out, f10rb.out, f10zr.out, f10raw.json

answers.answer: Not re-run in this session. Old firmware with the Python helper was covered by the C run: ~/e2e/hw2 has o100.pybtle, o100.pyzigbee and f10ab*.py logs for 1.0.0 and 1.2.0. A stock Kismet needs a stock build, which does not exist on the Pi. For the roll-up, the Python helper on the current firmware captured Wi-Fi on both bands, zigbee (TXTEST) and BTLE on the Pi; flashing was not repeated here.
answers.evidence: Coverage of the other checks in this session: p2-p21.

hardware_answers.question: Re-measure start and radio-switch times with the current helpers (with the 0.8 s MODE settle): a local source with the board already on the radio versus after a switch; Kismet start to first packets; one remote C helper hopping for 60 s (device counts).

answers.answer: Partial, C local. Launched->capturing is 1.05-1.50 s for the same radio and about 1.5 s for Wi-Fi<->802.15.4, BLE->Wi-Fi and Wi-Fi->BTLE, with 0.8 s of that the MODE settle. It is 2.5 s when the board USB re-enumerates, and in one case (n1) the BTLE switch failed entirely. Kismet start -> first Wi-Fi packet with two Wi-Fi boards: 2.20/2.20, 2.79/3.29 and 2.24/3.66 s. The Python helper took about 1 s from 'opened' to 'capturing'. The 60 s C-remote device count was not run.
answers.evidence: n1, n1b, n1c, g1a-c, g4 logs; rt-py-*.out.

answers.answer: Python helper radio switch, board 10:BD:A3:C8:7D:54 (the board whose Wi-Fi to BLE switch hung once under the C helper). All 25 switches succeeded. Opened to capturing, median: same radio 0.97 s, Wi-Fi to zigbee 1.23 s, zigbee to Wi-Fi 1.36 s, Wi-Fi to BTLE 1.23 s, BTLE to Wi-Fi 1.31 s. MODE to START gap: 0.80 s.
answers.evidence:
p12.out, min/median/max:
- wifi->wifi: start->capturing 1.07/1.23/1.52, opened->capturing 0.81/0.97/1.26.
- wifi->zigbee: 1.49/1.50/1.60, opened 1.23/1.23/1.34.
- zigbee->wifi: 1.62/1.62/1.68, opened 1.36/1.36/1.38.
- wifi->btle: 1.48/1.50/1.59, opened 1.21/1.23/1.34.
- btle->wifi: 1.54/1.57/1.61, opened 1.28/1.31/1.35.
No re-enumeration: 4 by-id links throughout.

The helper always sends MODE first, so even the same radio waits the 0.8 s settle. strace MODE->START: 0.803 s (p3) and 0.803 s (p8).

hardware_answers.question: Do both helpers behave the same for a board (names, UUID E5C5000M-...-<MAC> per radio, hardware label, channel= rules, port claims)? Does a by-id path give the MAC UUID in the Python helper? Is the board re-found by MAC on reopen, after a tty swap and after an unplug longer than 20 s?

answers.answer: Partial. The UUID per radio is identical across C local, C remote and Python remote (E5C5000M-0000-0000-0000-<MAC>, M=1/2/3), and so is the hardware label. A by-id path gives the MAC UUID in both helpers. A pty gets a path-hash UUID (E5C50001-...-C9B0E658C827). A local re-open after SIGKILL keeps the UUID. They differ in capture_interface (C 'esp32c5-<tty>', Python the path) and in the log shape: C '<name> capturing (wifi)', Python '<name> - /dev/ttyACM3 opened' / '... capturing'. tty swap, unplug and the Python 15 s give-up were not run.
answers.evidence: n1c, n8t, n9, n4r, n7, n15.

answers.answer:
Both helpers give a board the same identity: UUID E5C5000M-0000-0000-0000-<MAC> with M=1/2/3 for wifi/zigbee/btle, and the same hardware label. The Python helper gives the MAC UUID for a ttyACM name, a by-id link and a /tmp symlink alike.

The same board twice in one process is refused. After the 15 s give-up (download-mode trick), the source reconnects under the same UUID.

The tty swap and a true unplug over 20 s were not tested; they need a physical replug.
answers.evidence:
p2 and p9 d. 'Both want' texts, exit 2:
- 'esp32c5-ttyACM0 and esp32c5btle:device=/dev/serial/by-id/..._10:BD:A3:CF:05:40-if00 both want /dev/serial/by-id/..._10:BD:A3:CF:05:40-if00'
- 'esp32c5-ttyACM0 and esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM0 both want /dev/ttyACM0'
- 'esp32c5:device=/dev/ttyACM0 and esp32c5:device=<by-id> both want <by-id>'

p8: Kismet logged 'Matching new remote source 'esp32c5-ttyACM2' with known source with UUID 'E5C50001-0000-0000-0000-3844BEBFD80C'' and 'reconnected' after each give-up.

hardware_answers.question: What hardware label and capture interface do Kismet's REST API and UI show with the current helpers: 'Espressif USB-Serial-JTAG (<MAC>)', a C helper capif of esp32c5-ttyACM0, and the Python helper reporting the port?

answers.answer: The hardware label is 'Espressif USB-Serial-JTAG (<MAC>)' in all setups; a pseudo-terminal gets 'ESP32-C5'. The C helper reports capture_interface 'esp32c5-<tty>' for every radio and for by-id definitions: esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM1 -> 'esp32c5-ttyACM1', 'esp32c5:device=<by-id>' -> 'esp32c5-ttyACM0', C remote zigbee -> 'esp32c5-ttyACM2', pty -> 'esp32c5-pts/1'. The Python helper reports the port as given ('/dev/ttyACM3', or the full by-id path). A by-id definition gets the name/interface 'esp32c5', so the C local and Python by-id sources in n9 were both named 'esp32c5'.

For D8:0C, hardware was 'Espressif USB-Serial-JTAG (38:44:BE:BF:D8:0C)' for the C local, C remote and Python remote helpers alike. capture_interface was 'esp32c5-ttyACM2' for both C setups and '/dev/ttyACM2' for the Python helper. UUIDs follow the radio: E5C50001 (wifi), E5C50002 (zigbee), E5C50003 (btle), each -0000-0000-0000-3844BEBFD80C, and are the same in every helper.
answers.evidence: f10rb.out, f10zr.out, f10w.out, f10b.out (kq.py src lines)

answers.answer: The hardware string is 'Espressif USB-Serial-JTAG (<MAC>)' for all three setups: C local, C remote and Python. capture_interface is esp32c5-ttyACMn for the C helper, even for btle, zigbee and by-id definitions. For the Python helper it is the port as written: /dev/ttyACM0, the by-id path, or a /tmp symlink. interface is the definition's name part, for example esp32c5zigbee for 'esp32c5zigbee:device=...'.
answers.evidence: Files: p2.out (a/b/c) and p9.out (d: /tmp/py/board1 gave capture_interface '/tmp/py/board1' and UUID E5C50001-...-3844BEBFC910). Only REST was checked; no browser.

hardware_answers.question: On real boards with both helpers, does channel= set the start channel, and with channel_hop=false keep the source there (802.15.4 on 20, Wi-Fi on a 5 GHz channel, BTLE 37/38/39)? Do 200 TXTEST frames arrive as 200 packets of link type 230?

answers.answer: channel= with channel_hop=false works with all three helpers. zigbee channel=20 gave REST ch '20' hop 0, a single 'CHANNELS 20' with START, and TXTEST 200 -> exactly 200 packets of link type 230; devices 00:01 and FF:FF on channel 20, 2450000 kHz, +9 dBm. Wi-Fi channel=36 gave all 4813 packets at 5180 MHz. channel=36 without hop=false does not start on 36: the hop thread begins during the 0.8 s MODE settle and START went out with 'CHANNELS 13', then it hops. BTLE channel=38 is accepted but shows channel '37', hopping 1, hop_channels ['37','38'], and the helper tunes only 37. channel=200 gives 'esp32c5zigbee-ttyACM1: channel=200 is not a channel the board can tune to in zigbee mode' (typed). Re-adding a board/radio whose closed source record still exists is refused: 'Conflict of new datasource w48lock/E5C50001-...-10BDA3C87D54 and existing datasource w36hop with the same UUID'.
answers.evidence: glock/glock2 logs and strace (168599, 168637, 168648, 169587), glock.pcapng summary, glock2.devs.json, n4r, g3.

answers.answer:
With the Python helper, channel= plus channel_hop=false holds the channel. Zigbee on 20 received 200/200 frames. Wi-Fi on 36 put every frame at 5180 MHz. BTLE channel=38 is accepted but reported as 37.

Without channel_hop=false, channel=36 is not really visited at the start: Kismet's hop list reaches the helper before START, and the first START carried CHANNELS 13.

When a UUID is reused within one Kismet run, the old record's options stay. Going from hopping to locked works. Going from locked to a plain definition stays locked, with both remote helpers.

channel=200 is refused at start-up with exit 2.
answers.evidence:
Zigbee on 20, BTLE on 38 and the startup errors:
- Zigbee on 20: see check 3.
- BTLE channel=38: REST channel '37', hopping 1, hop_channels [37,38]; Kismet appended 38.
- BTLE channel=38,channel_hop=false: channel '37', hopping 0.
- Startup errors: 'python -m esp32c5_kismet.remote: error: esp32c5-ttyACM0:channel=200: esp32c5-ttyACM0: channel=200 is not a channel the board can tune to in wifi mode', exit 2. The same form for Wi-Fi 15, zigbee 30 and btle 40.

Wi-Fi channel=36 without channel_hop=false, in a fresh Kismet: REST shows channel 36 and hopping 1. strace shows CHANNELS 1, 5, 9, 13, then 'CHANNELS 13\nDWELL 250\nSTART'.

Reused UUID (p4b), in order:
1. 'lock36' (channel=36,channel_hop=false): locked.
2. Plain 'esp32c5-ttyACM0': definition still 'esp32c5-ttyACM0:channel=36,channel_hop=false,name=lock36', hopping 0, 1 CHANNELS write.
3. C remote, plain: the same.
4. ':channel_hop=true': hopping 1.
5. ':name=plain': definition becomes '...channel=36,channel_hop=true,name=plain'.
The OPENREQ carried Kismet's merged definition.

hardware_answers.question: Has TIOCEXCL landed? While a helper holds a board, does a second open fail with EBUSY/'already in use', is esptool refused, and does this hold for both helpers? This is what the container-vs-host warnings depend on.

answers.answer: TIOCEXCL has landed in both helpers. While either holds a board: os.open gives errno 16 EBUSY, pyserial fails with '[Errno 16] ... Device or resource busy', and esptool read-mac fails with 'Could not open ..., the port is busy or doesn't exist.' (exit 2). The capture is not disturbed. A second C source for another radio gets '... is already in use by another capture (an esp32c5 source or another program holds it); a board captures with one radio at a time'. A remote helper for the same board and radio is not refused locally, though: Kismet closes the running source, and the new helper takes over (see problems). Cross-container, per pi-docker-test.log D3: 'host open of /dev/ttyACM0 as osh: ERR 16 Device or resource busy', 'PASS D3 host open refused with EBUSY while the container captures', and the container's 4 sources kept running.
answers.evidence: n2b.out, n5b.out, g1a.log (208 s), pi-docker-test.log lines 26-38.

answers.answer: TIOCEXCL has landed in the Python helper as well: while it holds a board, every other open gets EBUSY, esptool is refused, and a second helper on another radio is refused with 'already in use'. The exception: a second helper with the same definition makes Kismet close the running one (check 4). The cross-container direction is in pi-docker-test.log D3 (not re-run).
answers.evidence: p5.out; see check 4. The Python-as-holder direction was also seen in the C run's n2b.out.

code_corrections.problem: Line 123 says only the Docker helper role restarts a remote helper after 'Could not probe'. Line 124's probe examples include 'esp32c5-<port>'. Line 127 ('The port') mentions only flock. Lines 222 and 230 (warning, VERIFY) say the lock does not cross containers. The page never mentions the capability drop.
code_corrections.correct: The framework retries every 5 s unless --disable-retry. The 'claimed while the board cannot be found' case is for names without a port (esp32c5, esp32c5zigbee, esp32c5-kitchen); a named port is claimed whether or not it exists. The helper sets TIOCEXCL after the flock (not on ptys), which holds across containers except against CAP_SYS_ADMIN. It drops every capability and sets no_new_privs first thing, even when installed setuid root, where it retries an EACCES open with the invoking user's fsuid. So containers need no NET_ADMIN.

code_corrections.problem: ~230: the flock lives on the device node, so the lock does not stop the host or a second container.
code_corrections.correct: Keep the flock explanation, and add TIOCEXCL, which the kernel keeps with the tty and so holds across containers (except for CAP_SYS_ADMIN; not on ptys).

code_corrections.problem: Line 123 says a portless definition stops the helper before it connects and that 'the Docker image's helper role starts it again every 5 s'.
code_corrections.correct: The framework's retry covers this case too: 'Could not probe local source ...' ends only the capture child, and the helper tries again 5 s later unless --disable-retry is given. The Docker loop is not involved.
